findings: The headline suggests lifting the bladder neck to Cooper’s ligament, which can imply direct apposition or excessive elevation.

The bladder and urethra are visibly disconnected at the neck. Isolated vaginal ovals and anchors at nearly the same longitudinal level do not clearly depict proximal urethral and bladder-neck support.
Original MDX wording to tie snugly reinforced excessive tension. The rewritten text uses gentle anatomic assessment and avoids a fixed recipe.
